extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners prosecuting reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for examining and prosecuting U.S. patent reissue applications, covering required oaths/declarations, ownership/assignee consents, amendments, terminal disclaimers, litigation effects, and common rejections under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration must identify an appropriate error
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration filed with this application is defective because none of the errors which are relied upon to support the reissue application are errors upon which a reissue can be based. See 37 CFR 1.175 and MPEP § 1414.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph when the reissue oath/declaration identifies only one error (or multiple errors) relied upon to support the reissue and that error (or none of the errors) is not an appropriate error upon which a reissue can be based. If at least one identified error is appropriate, do not use the 'none appropriate' paragraph. Form paragraph 14.14 must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 'without any deceptive intention' statement required (filed before Sept. 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration filed with this application, which has a filing date before September 16, 2012, is defective because it fails to contain a statement that all errors which are being corrected in the reissue application up to the time of filing of the oath/declaration arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant. See pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.175 and MPEP § 1414.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration must be received before the reissue application can be allowed. Example acceptable supplemental language is provided. Form paragraph 14.14 must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration must state patent is wholly or partly inoperative or invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration filed with this application is defective because it fails to contain the statement(s) required under 37 CFR 1.175 as to applicant's belief that the original patent is wholly or partly inoperative or invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when applicant fails to allege that the original patent is inoperative or invalid and/or fails to state the reason (defective specification/drawing or claiming more/less than the right). In the Office action, point out the specific defect and follow with form paragraph 14.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: General defect in reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration filed with this application is defective (see 37 CFR 1.175 and MPEP § 1414) because of the following: [explain defect].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the reissue oath/declaration does not comply with 37 CFR 1.175 and none of the specific form paragraphs 14.01.01–14.01.05 or 14.05.02 apply. Must be followed by an explanation of why defective and then form paragraph 14.14. Do not use in an examiner's amendment; supplemental oath/declaration must be filed prior to Notice of Allowability; do not use if no amendments have been made since last oath/declaration (then allow the case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration required prior to allowance (pre‑Sept. 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1), for applications filed before September 16, 2012, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration must be received before this reissue application can be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph to remind applicant of the requirement and provide example language for a supplemental oath/declaration. Form paragraph 14.14 must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation‑related reissue — material documents must be made of record
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent sought to be reissued by this application [1] involved in litigation. Any documents and/or materials which would be material to patentability of this reissue application are required to be made of record in response to this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is related to litigation, indicate that extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted during prosecution. In bracket 1 insert either 'is' or 'has been'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in reissue not stayed or suspended while related litigation is stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: While there is a stay of the concurrent litigation related to this reissue application, action in this reissue application will NOT be stayed or suspended because a stay of that litigation is in effect for the purpose of awaiting the outcome of these reissue proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted due to related litigation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in reissue not stayed when related litigation terminated
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the litigation related to this reissue application is terminated and final, action in this reissue application will NOT be stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted due to related litigation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in reissue not stayed when litigation issues do not overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: While there is concurrent litigation related to this reissue application, action in this reissue application will NOT be stayed because there are no significant overlapping issues between the application and that litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted due to related litigation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in reissue not stayed per applicant's request
rubrics_metrics.description: While there is concurrent litigation related to this reissue application, action in this reissue application will NOT be stayed because of applicant's request that the application be examined at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted due to related litigation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in reissue may be stayed due to concurrent litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of concurrent litigation, and in order to avoid duplication of effort between the two proceedings, action in this reissue application is STAYED until such time as it is evident to the examiner that (1) a stay of the litigation is in effect, (2) the litigation has been terminated, (3) there are no significant overlapping issues between the application and the litigation, or (4) applicant requests that the application be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when duplication of effort is likely; explains when stay may be lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminder of duties under 37 CFR 1.178(b) and 1.56
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is reminded of the continuing obligation under 37 CFR 1.178(b) to timely apprise the Office of any prior or concurrent proceeding in which Patent No. [1] is or was involved, and under 37 CFR 1.56 to timely apprise the Office of any information which is material to patentability of the claims under consideration in this reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These obligations rest with each individual associated with filing and prosecution. Use in the first action in a reissue application; insert patent number in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — 35 U.S.C. 251: Broadened claims after two years
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being broadened in a reissue application filed outside the two year statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is broader in scope than the original claims if it contains within its scope any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent; broadened if broader in any one respect even though narrower in others. Identify and explain claim limitations that broaden scope. See MPEP §§ 706.03(x) and 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — 35 U.S.C. 251: Broadened claims filed by assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being improperly broadened in a reissue application made and sworn to by the assignee. The application for reissue may be made and sworn to by the assignee of the entire interest only if the application does not seek to enlarge the scope of the claims of the original patent or (for reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012) the application for the original patent was filed by the assignee of the entire interest under 37 CFR 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is broader in scope if it contains any conceivable product/process not covered by the original patent. Identify limitations that broaden scope and explain. See MPEP §§ 706.03(x) and 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — Defective reissue oath or declaration (form paragraph 14.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as being based upon a defective reissue [2] under 35 U.S.C. 251 as set forth above. See 37 CFR 1.175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the nature of the defect(s) in the oath/declaration and require submission of a paper satisfying 37 CFR 3.73. In bracket 1 list all claims in reissue application; brackets 2 and 3 insert either --oath-- or --declaration--. This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 14.01 and appropriate subparagraphs and followed by guidance on correcting the defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent to reissue required (37 CFR 1.172(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is objected to under 37 CFR 1.172(a) as lacking the written consent of all assignees owning an undivided interest in the patent. The consent of the assignee must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.172. See MPEP § 1410.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper assent of the assignee in compliance with 37 CFR 1.172 and 3.73 is required in reply. If consent submitted is insufficient (not all assignees, conditional, or ineffective copy), explain following this form paragraph. If otherwise ready for allowance, follow with form paragraph 7.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee must establish ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is objected to under 37 CFR 1.172(a) as the assignee has not established its ownership interest in the patent for which reissue is being requested. An assignee must establish its ownership interest in order to support the consent to a reissue application required by 37 CFR 1.172(a). The assignee's ownership interest is established by: (a) filing evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee, or (b) specifying in the record of the reissue application where such evidence is recorded in the Office (e.g., reel and frame number, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when ownership is not established. If otherwise ready for allowance, follow with form paragraph 7.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission establishing ownership must be signed by an appropriate party
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership interest is informal. There is no indication of record that the party who signed the submission is an appropriate party to sign on behalf of the assignee. See 37 CFR 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper submission establishing ownership interest in the patent, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.172(a), is required in response. Follow with appropriate subparagraphs (14.16.02–14.16.04.fti) and optionally 14.16.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to state capacity to sign ownership submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who signed the submission establishing ownership interest has failed to state his/her capacity to sign for the corporation or other business entity, and he/she has not been established as being authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the submission establishing ownership may be signed by a patent practitioner of record (37 CFR 3.73; MPEP § 325). Use form paragraph 14.16.06 to explain how an official other than a recognized officer may properly sign. Inclusion of the person's title is desirable but not mandatory when employing certain options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of capacity to sign (signer not a recognized officer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who signed the submission establishing ownership interest is not recognized as an officer of the assignee, and he/she has not been established as being authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 324 (pre‑Sept. 16, 2012) and § 325 (on/after Sept. 16, 2012). Use appropriate following form paragraphs to explain and direct correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent of record may not sign ownership submission (pre‑Sept. 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership interest was signed by applicant's [1]. For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012, an attorney or agent of record is not authorized to sign a submission establishing ownership interest, unless he/she has been established as being authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. See MPEP § 324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, submission may be signed by a patent practitioner of record. While indication of person's title is desirable, inclusion is not mandatory when this option is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to accept ownership submission signed by non‑recognized officer
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be acceptable for a person, other than a recognized officer, to sign a submission establishing ownership interest, provided the record for the application includes a duly signed statement that the person is empowered to sign a submission establishing ownership interest and/or act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new submission including such an empowerment statement will be considered signed by an appropriate official. A separately filed paper referencing the previously filed submission and containing a proper empowerment statement is also acceptable. This form paragraph must be preceded by 14.16.02, 14.16.03 or 14.16.04.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — 35 U.S.C. 251: New matter added to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being based upon new matter added to the patent for which reissue is sought. The added material which is not supported by the prior patent is as follows: [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2, provide page and line numbers and explanation. Also make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph) if new matter is added to claims or specification affecting claims. If new matter added to specification not affecting claims, make an objection under 35 U.S.C. 132 using form paragraph 7.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to reissue must comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is notified that any subsequent amendment to the specification and/or claims must comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b). In addition, for reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012, when any substantive amendment is filed in the reissue application, which amendment otherwise places the reissue application in condition for allowance, a supplemental oath/declaration will be required. See MPEP § 1414.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in first Office action to advise proper manner of making amendments and need to file supplemental oath/declaration before allowance (for pre‑2012 filings). Improper amendments will be called out with a shortened statutory period for reply (one month or thirty days, whichever longer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment to reissue — 37 CFR 1.173(b) informality
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] proposes amendments to [2] that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b), which sets forth the manner of making amendments in reissue applications. A supplemental paper correctly amending the reissue application is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph may be used for any 37 CFR 1.173(b) informality as to an amendment submitted prior to final rejection. After final rejection, inform applicant that the amendment will not be entered by way of an Advisory Office action. When using, specify the proposed amendments not in compliance in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 251: No error without deceptive intention (external knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 251 because this application was filed before September 16, 2012 and error 'without any deceptive intention' has not been established. In view of the judicial determination in [2] of [3] on the part of applicant, a conclusion that any error was 'without deceptive intention' cannot be supported. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to point out judicial determinations of fraud/inequitable conduct/violation of duty of disclosure. Provide citation/location in opinion where determination is set forth. Do not use in applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 251: No error without deceptive intention (evidence in application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 251 because this application was filed before September 16, 2012 and error 'without any deceptive intention' has not been established. In view of the reply filed on [2], a conclusion that any error was 'without deceptive intention' cannot be supported. [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when admissions or evidence in the application's record indicate fraud/inequitable conduct. Admissions must be explicit and unequivocal. Do not use in applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer accepted when properly filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer filed on [1] disclaiming the terminal portion of any patent granted on this application which would extend beyond the expiration date of [2] has been reviewed and is accepted. The terminal disclaimer has been recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert filing date in bracket 1 and Patent/Application Number in bracket 2. See MPEP § 1490 for requirements. Use 14.23.01 for reexamination proceedings. For improper terminal disclaimers, see form paragraphs 14.24 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer not proper — introductory paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer filed on [1] disclaiming the terminal portion of any patent granted on this application which would extend beyond the expiration date of [2] has been reviewed and is NOT accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or more of form paragraphs 14.26 to 14.32 must follow to indicate reasons why not accepted. If disclaimer not accepted, provide guidance on replacement/supplemental disclaimer and fees (form paragraph 14.35). Do not use in reexamination proceedings; use 14.25 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer defects — extent of interest not stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who has signed the disclaimer has not stated the extent of his/her interest, or the business entity's interest, in the application/patent. See 37 CFR 1.321(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26. Use when signer fails to state owner's extent of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer directed to particular claim(s) (not acceptable)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is directed to a particular claim or claims, which is not acceptable, since 'the disclaimer must be of a terminal portion of the term of the entire [patent or] patent to be granted.' See MPEP § 1490.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26. Provide example of proper terminal disclaimer language using form paragraphs 14.27.04.fti or 14.27.04.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer not signed or improperly identified
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer was not signed; or the application/patent being disclaimed has not been identified; or the application/patent being disclaimed has been improperly identified since the number used is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply correct identification and date. Must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26. If number incorrect, insert correct Application or Patent Number and explain correction methods. See associated examiner notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer not signed by all owners (pre‑Sept. 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application was filed before September 16, 2012. The terminal disclaimer was not signed by all owners and, therefore, supplemental terminal disclaimers are required from the remaining owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26. Do not use this paragraph for applications filed on/after Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer fee not submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer fee of $ [1] in accordance with 37 CFR 1.20(d) has not been submitted, nor is there any authorization in the application file to charge a specified Deposit Account or credit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert fee amount in bracket 1. Must be preceded by 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26. If fee was paid for a disclaimer later rejected, applicant does not have to pay another fee for a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer signing capacity and identification issues (post‑Sept. 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012: the person who signed the terminal disclaimer may not be the applicant, the patentee or an attorney or agent of record; the person may have failed to state capacity to sign; or the party identified may not be the applicant of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signer not proper, cite 37 CFR 1.321(a) and (b). To be reconsidered, the terminal disclaimer must be filed with a request to change applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c) including an application data sheet and comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73. Use appropriate follow-on form paragraphs (14.24/14.25 and 14.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must include enforceable‑only‑during‑common‑ownership clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer must include a recitation that any patent granted shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent is commonly owned with the application(s) or patent(s) which formed the basis for the double patenting rejection. See 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must include 37 CFR 1.321(d) waiver for joint research agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not include the waiver and enforceability provisions of 37 CFR 1.321(d). The terminal disclaimer must include a provision: (1) waiving the right to separately enforce (a) any patent granted on that application or the patent being reexamined and (b) the reference patent, or any patent granted on the reference application which formed the basis for the double patenting rejection; and (2) agreeing that any patent granted on that application or patent being reexamined shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent and the reference patent ... are not separately enforced. See 37 CFR 1.321(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012, follow with form paragraphs 14.27.07.fti or 14.27.08; for applications on/after Sept. 16, 2012, follow with 14.27.07.1 or 14.27.08. Precede with 14.24/14.25 AND 14.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture prohibition in reissue (impermissible recapture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being an impermissible recapture of broadened claimed subject matter surrendered in the application for the patent upon which the present reissue is based. A broadening aspect is present in the reissue which was not present in the application for patent. The record shows that the broadening aspect relates to claimed subject matter that applicant previously surrendered during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain specifics why recapture exists, omitted/broadened claim limitations providing the 'broadening aspect', and where in the original application the narrowed claim scope was presented/argued to obviate a rejection/objection. See MPEP § 1412.02 and cited case law (Greenliant, Mostafazadeh, North American Container, Pannu, Hester, etc.).
